learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to report what someone said exactly as they said it or by turning it into a smooth story of your own!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Direct Speech is when we repeat the exact words a person said. We always trap these words inside magical quotation marks! For example: Rahul said, 'I love playing cricket.'

Indirect Speech is when we report what someone said without using their exact words. We remove the quotation marks and usually add the word 'that'. For example: Rahul said that he loved playing cricket.
When we change Direct to Indirect speech, the tense usually takes one step back into the past! 'I am happy' (Present) becomes 'She said that she was happy' (Past).
Pronouns also change when we report speech to match who is telling the story. 'I' becomes 'he' or 'she', and 'my' becomes 'his' or 'her'.

fun_activity.title: 🎤 The News Reporter Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Ask your sibling or friend to say one sentence about their favorite food. First, write down exactly what they said using quotation marks, then rewrite it as a news report using Indirect Speech!

quick_recap: ⭐ Direct Speech uses quotation marks to show the exact words spoken by someone.
⭐ Indirect Speech reports the meaning of what was said without quotes, often changing the tense and pronouns.
